Europe Pushes Back

European counterparts have pushed back sharply on reopening that channel, according to The New York Times report, because it would reverse years of European Union policy aimed at cutting dependence on Russian supply. The White House, in a statement, said the war was "driving up energy prices across Europe and creating significant economic hardship in both Russia and Ukraine."

Europe’s import mix has already shifted, with Russian gas accounting for 13% of E.U. gas imports last year versus 45% in 2021. Still, people familiar with the talks said Trump officials believe European voters will keep pressuring leaders for lower energy costs, making Russian supply tempting if a ceasefire deal emerges.
In Washington, criticism of Trump’s sanctions step spilled across party lines even as his team discussed energy-related incentives in diplomacy. Sen.
Thom Tillis
(R-N.C.) called the waiver "beyond irresponsible," and Sen.
Richard Blumenthal
(D-Conn.) called it a "craven, cowardly action" after Congress passed the legislation last month.
